text:
Ty Emberson's value has always been hard to see from the scoresheet, and this season is no different: two assists in 14 games at about 12 minutes a night, as a right shot on Edmonton's third pair. His second assist came on Nov. 7 against Vancouver.

The case for him lives in last season's numbers. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.4 wins above replacement, nearly all of it from defending at even strength, with opponents creating fewer chances when he was out there (89th percentile). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agrees that offense isn't where he earns his keep.

This year's five-on-five results are weaker. With Emberson on the ice, the Oilers get 37% of the shot attempts and 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), seven points worse than the team without him. They've also scored about two and a half more goals than those chances predicted during his shifts, which is luck working in his favour and unlikely to last. If his chances against come back to last season's level, he's a useful depth defenseman. If they don't, the good bounces are hiding a slide.
headline: Ty Emberson, quiet value and some kind bounces
